issues.legal_issue: The compulsory joinder of multiple mortgage claims applies only when the same mortgagor executed the mortgages being enforced.
material_facts: The appellant alone executed the earlier mortgage sued upon in the current proceeding.
The mortgages involved in the earlier suit were executed by the appellant and his wife, who each mortgaged a separately owned property.
The bank had obtained and satisfied a decree in the earlier suit before suing on the mortgage executed by the appellant alone.
issues.conclusion: The earlier suit did not bar the bank from bringing a separate suit on the mortgage executed by the appellant alone because the mortgagors were not the same.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 61 and 67A of the Transfer of Property Act, a mortgagee who sues on one of multiple mortgages executed by the same mortgagor and carrying a right to the same kind of decree must, absent a contrary contract, sue on all mortgages whose money is due. The section requires the mortgagor to be the same; a husband and wife who own distinct properties and mortgage them separately are not treated as one entity. The court approved and applied Moro Raghunath v. Balaji, I.L.R. 13 Bom. 45.

predicates.mortgagee_sues_to_enforce_one_of_multipl: A mortgagee brings a proceeding to enforce one of multiple mortgages made in its favour.
predicates.same_mortgagor_across_mortgages: The same person or persons executed each mortgage being considered for enforcement.

issues.definition: When a mortgagee sues to enforce one of multiple mortgages and the mortgagor is not the same across those mortgages, separate enforcement is not barred by compulsory joinder.

issues.legal_issue: A mortgage interest rate that is unfair and penal in light of the mortgage terms and the circumstances may be reduced.
material_facts: The mortgage provided for interest at the original contractual rate and a higher rate following default.
The trial court applied the higher rate of 12% before the preliminary decree.
The Supreme Court assessed the mortgage deed and all the circumstances and found the 12% rate unfair and penal.
issues.conclusion: The Court reduced interest before the preliminary decree to the original contractual rate of 10.5%, while leaving in place the trial court's direction for 6% interest thereafter until realization.
issues.legal_principle: Considering the provisions of the mortgage deed and all the circumstances, the Court held that the applied rate was unfair and penal and reduced it. The Usurious Loans Act, 1918 was raised as a defence, but the judgment does not set out a specific statutory test or further interpret that Act.

predicates.mortgage_enforcement_proceeding: A proceeding seeks enforcement of a debt secured by a mortgage.
predicates.interest_rate_is_unfair_and_penal_in_lig: The court finds, in light of the mortgage terms and surrounding circumstances, that the applied interest rate is unfair and penal.

issues.definition: In a mortgage enforcement proceeding, if the court finds the applied interest rate unfair and penal in light of the deed and circumstances, that rate is reduced.
